# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit

**Evidence standard.** This is a source-led audit. “Not documented” means I did not find a defensible value in the fetched sources; it is not a claim that the tool cannot do it. URLs are attached to every factual claim.

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow | Top 3 pain points | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Open audio; add/move markers; optionally import MIDI/clipboard; preview slices; copy BMSE or iBMSC marker data; copy/append keysound list; export WAV keysounds. README documents BMHelper compatibility and project save/load. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features), [shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts)) | iBMSC high-resolution data can yield missing keysounds or gamemode changes after save; zero-crossing reduces clicks but moves timing; BPM-change support is only partial/hackish. ([notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes), [planned work](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features)) | Snap 1/1–1/192; BMSE copy rounds to nearest 192th. No slice-count ceiling is stated. ([features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)) | Clipboard to BMSE/iBMSC; keysound list clipboard/BMS append; physical keysound export. ([shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts)) |
| **Woslicer II** | Load WAV, set BPM/grid, place cut points, export chopped WAVs and clipboard/sequence data for BMSE. A guide describes II/III as WAV chopping support tools. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer)) | Keyboard/UI differences complicate II↔III migration; unsupported WAVs can force-close; the documented workaround is resaving through SoundEngine Free/Audacity and checking for 24/32-bit exports. ([wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer), [comparison](http://yuinore.net/2017/04/otokiri-software/)) | The fetched II/III docs do not state a numeric maximum. The Japanese Woslicer III guide documents grid resolution up to 192 divisions per measure. ([guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)) | “Total output” creates many WAV files; clipboard output is pasted into BMSE. ([workflow guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| **Woslicer III** | Either direct “ぶつ切り” (manual point-by-point chopping) or BMHelper-assisted: export transformed MIDI, render audio, copy cut positions from BMHelper, clipboard-import them into Woslicer, set BPM, total-export, then define WAVs and paste sequence into BMSE. ([workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Antivirus detection/removal prevented at least one user from launching III; UI/operations differ from II; boundary processing can produce a pop and parallel-rendered tracks force a fade trade-off (shortened sound vs next-note bleed). ([comparison](http://yuinore.net/2017/04/otokiri-software/), [technical analysis](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)) | Documented Woslicer III grid: up to 192 per measure; no total-slice ceiling found. ([guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)) | Total WAV export plus Woslicer clipboard output to BMSE. ([workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| **BMHelper** | Export MIDI from DAW; split/group notes; render the generated MIDI to audio; copy cut positions; slice externally; copy definitions and sequence into BMSE. It does not slice audio itself. ([BMHelper docs](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html), [workflow](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) | FL Studio users may need to export each piano-roll part separately; definition clipboard had a beta line-break bug; clipboard data disappears when BMHelper closes and placement starts at the current measure/BGM lane, with a warning about measure #000. ([workflow](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) | No global max found. Practical controls include head padding, minimum interval, similarity tolerances, sorting, and multi-definition behavior. ([workflow](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) | External WAV slicing (Edison/Woslicer/etc.), then definition and sequence clipboard into BMSE. ([BMHelper docs](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html)) |
| **Mid2BMS** | MIDI/MML-to-BMS-oriented generation and WaveSplitter-style slicing; troubleshoot filename/audio correspondence in BMSE/iBMSC. ([troubleshooting](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/TIPS/%E9%9F%B3%E5%88%87%E3%82%8A%E3%81%AB%E5%A4%B1%E6%95%97%E3%81%97%E3%81%9F%E3%82%89)) | Velocity-0 notes disappear from MIDI; keyswitches are not directly usable; quiet/no-output notes and evolving FX fail automated slicing; silence threshold can over-split or merge sounds. ([troubleshooting](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/TIPS/%E9%9F%B3%E5%88%87%E3%82%8A%E3%81%AB%E5%A4%B1%E6%95%97%E3%81%97%E3%81%9F%E3%82%89)) | For BPM >200, the guide recommends MarginTime ≈ BPM/10; no overall slice maximum found. ([troubleshooting](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/TIPS/%E9%9F%B3%E5%88%87%E3%82%8A%E3%81%AB%E5%A4%B1%E6%95%97%E3%81%97%E3%81%9F%E3%82%89)) | Generated WAV/definitions and BMS-oriented output; exact exporter details vary by mode. ([wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/)) |
| **sound-slicer** | Put source samples/text and working BMS in a `wav` subfolder; read `.txt`, slice source WAV, generate a BMS clipboard file. Rhythmic mode emits one slice per MIDI event; melodic mode groups by note/length/velocity and requires re-rendering. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#sound-slicer)) | Rhythmic mode can create 1,000 slices for 1,000 notes and slight gaps; melodic mode has a multi-step render/slice/paste round trip; both modes do not support BPM changes. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#miditext)) | No numeric max; no snap denominator beyond the input MIDI/text behavior is documented. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#miditext)) | Physical WAV files plus generated BMS clipboard. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#sound-slicer)) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline / timing

| Severity | Problem | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Timing and audio-cleanliness conflict: zero-crossing moves markers, while iBMSC preserves arbitrary resolution; resulting saves can lose keysounds or change gamemode. | Sayaslicer explicitly documents this failure and recommends BMSE clipboard as a workaround. ([notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)) A non-destructive editor should preserve the authored time and expose a separate playback/export boundary adjustment. |
| P0 | BPM changes are not a first-class shared timeline. | Sayaslicer calls partial BPM support “a bit hackish” and lists proper grid/BMSE BPM support as planned; sound-slicer says both modes do not support BPM changes. ([Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#miditext)) |
| P1 | Manual chopping of parallel-rendered audio cannot simultaneously preserve the whole tail and exclude the next sound. | The Woslicer technical analysis describes the fade-before-cut/bleed-after-cut trade-off. ([Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)) |
| P1 | Boundary extension can introduce a pop. | Woslicer III’s reverse/inverted tail process inserts a one-sample zero at the fold point; the analysis identifies that as the pop source. ([Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)) |
| P1 | High-resolution grids are not safely round-tripped. | BMSE clipboard rounds to 192th; ubmsc’s default 192 partition can snap finer events and trigger overlap warnings. ([Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features), [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/#make-sure-your-maximum-grid-partition-is-high-enough-in-ubmsc)) |

### Interface / workflow

| Severity | Problem | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Traditional workflow has many handoffs: DAW → MIDI helper → DAW render → slicer → file manager → BMSE definitions → BMSE sequence paste. | This is the documented BMHelper/Woslicer flow, including re-opening tools and clipboard transfer. ([workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) A Slice Library and direct chart preview remove the most error-prone handoffs. |
| P1 | File ordering and starting selection are hidden state. | Woslicer/BMSE guidance says explorer order and the selected starting definition determine WAV numbering, and both must be aligned. ([workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| P1 | Clipboard lifetime and paste location are fragile. | BMHelper clipboard disappears when the app closes; sequence paste begins at current measure/BGM-lane left edge; measure #000 placement can cause play problems. ([BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) |
| P1 | Tool migration is not seamless. | II/III UI and operation differences hinder migration; one user reports III was removed by antivirus and stayed on II. ([comparison](http://yuinore.net/2017/04/otokiri-software/)) |
| P1 | Input compatibility is poor and errors are destructive-looking. | Woslicer may force-close on WAVs from Studio One/24–32-bit exports; the workaround is an external resave. ([wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer)) |

### Settings / controls

| Severity | Problem | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Users must tune multiple unrelated thresholds to avoid wrong grouping. | BMHelper exposes minimum interval, head padding, note/gate/velocity tolerances, and multi-definition intervals; Mid2BMS exposes MarginTime and silence detection where too low splits and too high merges. ([BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [Mid2BMS](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/TIPS/%E9%9F%B3%E5%88%87%E3%82%8A%E3%81%AB%E5%A4%B1%E6%95%97%E3%81%97%E3%81%9F%E3%82%89)) |
| P1 | Fade/tail behavior is not transparent. | Woslicer’s reverse/invert tail behavior and its fade trade-off are documented only in explanatory analysis, not as a safe, reversible per-slice preview. ([Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)) |
| P2 | Requested settings in the proposed DJMax design are not supported by the evidence as existing-tool features. | The fetched sources document snap, offset, fadeout, silent-tail removal, zero-crossing, undo/redo in Sayaslicer, but do **not** establish a Sayaslicer “Sensitivity 0.55”, per-slice Normalize, or Auto-advance Grid/Beat/Off control. ([Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)) Treat these as product hypotheses, not validated conventions. |

### Backend / packaging

| Severity | Problem | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Exporting hundreds of physical files creates naming, definition, size, and packaging work. | sound-slicer’s example has numbered WAVs in a `wav` folder; BMS checklist says WAV keysounds can be “ridiculously large,” recommends OGG and ~40MB total, and requires folder packaging. ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#project-layout), [checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/#please-convert-your-keysounds-to-ogg)) |
| P1 | Long keysounds have distribution limits. | LR2 submission guidance blocks keysounds over 60s and recommends splitting long vocals into about 40s segments. ([checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/#no-keysound-should-exceed-60s-in-length)) |
| P1 | Identifier capacity/compatibility is a moving target. | NamuWiki reports 255 in older systems, BMS’s 36-base range up to 1295, and BMSE’s Feb 2024 pilot base-62 expansion to 3843; this makes an explicit project-level identifier policy necessary. ([key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) |
| P1 | Engine playback semantics can cut tails or restart reused samples. | NamuWiki describes older single-sample-per-track interception and BMS-style same-number replay/restart behavior; Technica 2 moved to non-interfering inputs. ([key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) |
| P1 | Large source-file handling itself can fail. | Sayaslicer issue #5 reports >2GB loading lag/unusability from a signed-int buffer overflow; it was later fixed. ([issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5)) |

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer — keep these

1. **Preserve the familiar Woslicer keyboard model while adding layout-aware shortcuts.** Sayaslicer states shortcuts are the same as Woslicer II while accounting for keyboard layout. ([shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts))
2. **Offer both BMSE and iBMSC clipboard paths.** This recognizes real ecosystem interoperability, while explicitly warning when iBMSC is unsafe. ([features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features), [notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes))
3. **Keep zero-crossing optional and explain the timing trade-off.** It addresses clicks without pretending it is free. ([notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes))
4. **Add undo/redo, project save/load, marker copy/paste, arbitrary snap, and keysound-list export.** These directly reduce the repeated export/clipboard ceremony. ([features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features))
5. **Retain Woslicer’s direct manual chopping for non-MIDI/automation material.** The Woslicer guide identifies direct chopping as the fallback when MIDI/BMHelper does not work. ([workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
6. **Keep BMHelper interoperability.** BMHelper’s “copy cut positions” is specifically designed for Woslicer-style slicing, and Sayaslicer supports BMSE clipboard data. ([BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html), [Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features))

## 4. Top 10 recommendations for DJMax Studio Slicer

1. **P0 — Make slices virtual by default; export only on finalize.** This directly removes the documented render/slice/file-definition ceremony in the BMHelper/Woslicer workflow. ([workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
2. **P0 — Build a dual timeline: waveform/ms ruler below and chart/grid ruler above.** BPM changes are explicitly weak in Sayaslicer and unsupported in sound-slicer, so show both absolute time and musical position and keep them linked. ([Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#miditext))
3. **P0 — Separate authored boundaries from playback/export boundaries.** Zero-crossing should be a non-destructive per-slice offset/preview, because existing zero-crossing moves markers and can break iBMSC round-trips. ([notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes))
4. **P0 — Add an always-visible chart preview with auto-created notes and a reversible “Import to Studio” action.** This replaces clipboard paste location, definition numbering, and hidden starting-selection state documented in BMHelper/Woslicer workflows. ([BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
5. **P1 — Use a Slice Library with stable IDs, source ranges, reuse count, and warnings.** BMS identifiers range from 255/1295-era constraints to BMSE’s 3843 base-62 pilot, while repeated-note workflows deliberately reuse definitions. ([key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음), [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html))
6. **P1 — Provide snap presets 1/4–1/192 plus explicit “free/ms” mode and a resnap preview.** Sayaslicer supports 1/1–1/192 and BMSE rounds to 192, while finer divisions can be altered on save. ([Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features), [checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/#make-sure-your-maximum-grid-partition-is-high-enough-in-ubmsc))
7. **P1 — Make auto-advance, fade, tail, zero-X, and normalize previewable per slice, with global defaults and overrides.** Existing tools expose thresholds and fade/tail behavior but force users to infer outcomes from exported audio; Woslicer’s fade trade-off is a concrete reason. ([Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71), [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html))
8. **P1 — Add format validation and actionable repair.** Detect unsupported WAV bit depth, sample rate/channel layout, huge files, and >60s slices before export; existing users are told to resave in Audacity/SoundEngine or split long keysounds. ([Woslicer wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer), [Sayaslicer issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5), [checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/#no-keysound-should-exceed-60s-in-length))
9. **P1 — Support BMS / RESPECT / TECHNIKA mode semantics explicitly.** NamuWiki describes track interception/restart in older systems and non-interfering playback from Technica 2; the mode switch should warn about tail-cut behavior and same-ID replay. ([key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음))
10. **P2 — Make export a validated package operation, not “hundreds of WAVs.”** Offer WAV/OGG finalization, deterministic names, identifier-budget preview, manifest, and round-trip re-import. Packaging and OGG size are current BMS checklist concerns. ([checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/#zip-the-bms-in-a-folder), [checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/#please-convert-your-keysounds-to-ogg))

### Proposed feature verdict

**Dual timeline + chart preview + mode switcher + Import to Studio is validated as a strong direction by the failure modes, but not as an existing-tool pattern.** The sources show separate waveform slicing and chart/clipboard tools, BPM/grid gaps, hidden paste state, and export/package burdens; they do not show a conventional tool that keeps virtual ranges and notes in one reversible project. The non-destructive model should therefore be positioned as a direct fix for the documented handoffs, not as a feature already proven by Woslicer/Sayaslicer. ([Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features), [Woslicer workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html))
